lessonTitle: 36. The complex plane and trigonometric form
lessonTitleEnglish: The complex plane and trigonometric form
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 10 mathematics textbooks (advanced stream)

stages.headline: z = a + bi is drawn as the point (a; b); its modulus is the distance to the origin |z| = √(a² + b²), its argument the angle α with Ox.
stages.headlineEnglish: z = a + bi is drawn as the point (a; b); its modulus is the distance to the origin |z| = √(a² + b²), its argument the angle α with Ox.

stages.headline: Since a = r cos α and b = r sin α, the trigonometric form is z = r(cos α + i sin α), r = |z|.
stages.headlineEnglish: Since a = r cos α and b = r sin α, the trigonometric form is z = r(cos α + i sin α), r = |z|.

stages.headline: When multiplying, moduli multiply and arguments add; de Moivre: zⁿ = rⁿ(cos nα + i sin nα).
stages.headlineEnglish: When multiplying, moduli multiply and arguments add; de Moivre: zⁿ = rⁿ(cos nα + i sin nα).
